questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Appropriate courses available. The student climbing club.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I'm glad i went on exchange and experienced living in a new place. I feel I didn't manage to get the most out of the opportunity, though. Having chosen difficult courses, I didn't manage to invest much time into getting to know Dutch students. Even then, I would advise others to give it a go!

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. Almost everything was automatically sent to me by email, or written on websites linked to in those emails. While it was easy, it did end up taking me a lot of time.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A bunch of useful emails. And there were some informational intro days.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
I stayed with SSH. Short Stay Housing.
sshxl.nl
. I had a private apartment. They also offer shared apartments.
This was great. Only problem is, that many people weren't lucky enough to get SSH housing. You sign up using an online form, and then on a specified date and time, you basically have to click on a button before too many others click on the button.
Utrecht was in a student housing crisis. Some students even had to stay on campsites or hostels for a long time, until they found a place. Many Dutch people said, that the university had simply invited more international students than there was room for. You should try to have a Plan B, if you aren't lucky enough to get an SSH apartment.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I had my own small kitchen. This was possible, because I lived on the campus of University College Utrecht. Not in the Science Park. Most SSH apartments have a shared kitchen.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There was a great atmosphere on the University College Utrecht campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing was good, but there was not enough of it.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Pretty easy, but like everything administrative and bureaucratic, it just took a long time.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
UU has a website where you can look up courses. The Dutch universities have united to offer shared master-level courses in Mathematics. Those courses use another website,
elo.mastermath.nl
. It was a combination of using those websites and using the Erasmus websites (linked to and explained in the automatic emails). I made a priority list of courses on the Erasmus website and someone from UU signed me up.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Someone at UU replied to my emails, when I was in doubt of anything. You will be given a contact automatically.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Expect it to take some time to sort through the possible courses and fill out the documents.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two BA courses and two MA courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very similar, actually. In the masters courses, the exercise sessions didn't have time for working on the problems.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BA: Analysis on Manifolds
BA: Concurrency
MA: Commutative Algebra
MA: Algebraic Geometry 1

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Analysis on Manifolds was fun. Algebraic Geometry was quite fun. All the courses were fun. My lecturers were well qualified and gave good lectures. Maybe especially good lecturers in Algebraic Geometry 1 and Analysis on Manifolds.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to buy a bunch of kitchen equipment, as not all of the basic things were present.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Their standard supermarkets are a bit more expensive than what I'm used to. If you are willing to travel outside the city center, you can find cheaper options like LIDL/ALDI.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have multiple student sports associations. Student associations are taken much more seriously down here compared to Denmark. They also have some kind of semi-academic student associations, which I never really figured out.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I participated in the student climbing/alpine club, USAC. That was fantastic. They gave every member a group and a mentor, so we could easily get to know some people. Almost everyone was Dutch, but they were willing to speak English in my group. They also took us on an outdoor climbing trip, which was definitely one of the best experiences of my exchange.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
- Go on a bike trip to the northern outskirts of Utrecht. You will see the famous very flat fields, and how they drain them. Maybe some old windmills.
- Utrecht has a beautiful old city center. Go for a walk along the canals.
- Take a day-trip by train (or overnight by bike!) to Amsterdam. It's way more touristy, but also interesting. The van Gogh Museum was a memorable experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
The culture is not that different from the Danish culture. Much like in Denmark, most people are not very outgoing, so it's mostly on you, to get to know people. That was difficult for me.
There were some funny differences, which I felt no need to adjust to. Like people feeling embarrassed about wearing rain jackets/pants. And almost no dutchies wearing bicycle helmets.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Try to find a sports club. That was where I had most success.
On campus, they have no obvious shared place where math students like to go to. After lectures, people dissipate in every direction with each of their little friend groups. You might need to be really proactive, if you want to talk to your fellow students.
If you like partying, then join Erasmus Student Network (ESN) which is very active in Utrecht.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not sure if it's cultural, but I had a hard time with the lack of someplace specific, I could go, to find other math students.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Biking is in their blood. And they can be very direct.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Time will go by quickly. Choose interesting courses, but don't give yourself too much work to do. With all the practical things to figure out, you will probably feel like you have less time than back home, not more.
It's important to give yourself time and a surplus of energy, to reach out to new people. And to go explore your host country.
I truly enjoy my study, and like working on hard courses. But on an exchange stay like this, the social experiences are more important. They are what you are going to treasure most, when your stay is over.
I've never heard anyone complain about choosing courses that were too easy, during their exchange. I've had multiple people advise me, to prioritize time towards social experiences. I wish I had listened even more!
Go make the most of it. Do the things you can't do at home, with the people you won't meet at home. Enjoy your stay. Grab the it with both hands!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just really spend the time to make sure you will have housing.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The climbing club. Trying to live in a different country.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: You should go :) Go make the most of it. Do the things you can't do at home, with the people you won't meet at home. Enjoy your stay. Grab it with both hands!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
